Home / Repairs

Repairs and maintenance, handled

Plumbing, heating, electrical and general repairs, dealt with by a pre-vetted contractor network, with every job recorded as an invoice.

In an emergency, do not wait for a form

Gas leak or smell of gas: leave the property, do not use switches or flames, and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999.

Fire, flooding that risks life, or any immediate danger: call 999.

What we deal with

Four main areas of repair

Plumbing

Leaks, blockages, taps, toilets and pipework.

Heating

Boiler faults, radiators and hot water problems.

Electrical

Faulty sockets, lighting and electrical faults.

General repairs

Doors, windows, locks and everyday upkeep.

Trades covered: Plumbing, heating, electrical and general repairs. Our contractors are pre-vetted, and we do not publish names here.

The repair workflow

From report to rent statement

  1. Tenant reports the problem to GETLET.
  2. GETLET checks the management type. Fully Managed: we order directly. Limited Management: we ask you first.
  3. A contractor attends from the pre-vetted network.
  4. The invoice is added to PayProp against your property.
  5. The cost is deducted from the next rent and appears on your statement.

See a boiler fault in both plans

Our service standard

What the 24-hour standard means

This is GETLET's stated service standard. It is not an independently verified guarantee, and it does not mean every issue is fixed within 24 hours. The definitions below explain how it is applied.

When the clock starts

From the moment GETLET receives and logs the report.

Emergency versus routine

Emergencies are escalated immediately and the property is made safe first. Routine repairs are acknowledged, assessed and scheduled.

Access to the property

Time spent arranging access with the tenant is not counted as contractor delay.

Parts delays

If a part has to be ordered, we agree a revised plan with you and keep the tenant informed.

Landlord approval time (Limited Management)

In Limited Management the time taken to give approval sits outside our control and extends the timeline.

Escalation

Jobs that miss the standard are escalated to a senior member of the team and the reason is recorded.

In plain terms: capacity, access to the property and parts availability can all affect how long a repair takes. In Limited Management, the time you take to approve the work is an extra factor. Out-of-hours handling: Out-of-hours reports follow the emergency route on this page, and the arrangements for each plan are set out in your management agreement.

What happens next

  1. GETLET checks which management plan applies.
  2. A contractor is booked, or we ask the landlord first in Limited Management.
  3. You are kept updated until the job is done.
